full_judgment:
SM Maniruzzaman, j: In this Rule Nisi, issued under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, the respondents have been called upon to show cause as to why the impugned order dated 3-6-2021 passed by the Customs, Excise and VAT Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka (in short, the Tribunal), respondent No. 1 under Nathi No. সিইভিটি/কেইস(কাস)-১৭৮/২০২১/১২৫১ dismissing the appeal filed by the petitioner under section 196A of the Customs Act, 1969 (in short, the Act, 1969) against the adjudication order dated 29-9-2020 passed by the respondent No. 2 as being barred by limitation (Annexure-H), should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and hence, of no legal effect and or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said adjudication order dated 29-9-2020, the petitioner as appellant preferred customs appeal before the respondent No. 1, Tribunal which was registered as Nathi No. কাস/১৭৮/২০২১ dated 25-3-2021 along with filed an application under section 196A (5) of the Act, 1969 for condonation of delay of 86 days in preferring appeal. However, the respondent No. 1 fixed the matter on 24-5-2021 for hearing of the delay application and after hearing the petitioner, the Tribunal dismissed the appeal as barred by limitation vide its order dated 30-5-2021. 

 7. Mr Kazi Akhtar Hosain, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that section 196A(5) of the Act, 1969 having given authority to the Tribunal to admit the appeal presented beyond the stipulated time subject to showing sufficient cause and that the petitioner did show sufficient cause for not presenting the same in due time, but the Tribunal without properly applying it's discretionary power had rejected the application for condonation of delay and thereby dismissed the appeal as being time barred. He next submits that section 196A (5) of the Act, 1969 has empowered the respondent No. 1, Tribunal to admit the appeal even if the same has been filed beyond the period of limitation as prescribed under section 196A(3) of the said Act but the Tribunal did not apply its judicial mind, particularly did not exercise the discretion given in its favour under section 196A(5) of the said Act in passing the impugned order. Hence, the impugned order is liable to be declared to have been passed without any lawful authority. He further submits that due to Covid-19 pandemic prevailing at that time in Bangladesh normal works of all government/non-government offices have been hampered, as such the respondent No. 1 ought to have considered the delay of only 86 days in filing the appeal. In view of the said context, he submits that the impugned order is liable to be declared illegal and without lawful authority. He lastly submits that the Tribunal failed to look into the positive evidence in respect of delay in filing the appeal and passed the impugned order dismissing the appeal; thus, has failed to exercise its jurisdiction vested under section 196A(5) of the Act, 1969. In view of the above facts, he submits that the Rule should be made absolute and the delay of 86 days in filing appeal should be condoned. 

 8. On the other hand, Md Abul Kalam Khan Daud, the learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the respondent No. 2 without filing any affidavit-in-opposition submits that there is no illegality in the impugned order passed by the Tribunal, since the petitioner failed to explain any valid reason as to the delay in filing the appeal before the Tribunal. Having considered the said facts of the case, the Tribunal rightly dismissed the appeal as barred by limitation. 

 19. The impugned order dated 3-6-2021 passed by the respondent No. 1, under Nathi No. সিইভিটি/কেইস (কাস)-১৭৮/২০২১/১২৫১ dismissing the appeal filed by the petitioner under section 196A of the Customs Act, 1969 against the adjudication order dated 29-9-2020 passed by the respondent No. 2 as being barred by limitation (Annexure-H) is hereby declared to have been passed without lawful authority and hence, of no legal effect.
